title: King + pawn vs king
tagline: The escort, the blockade, and the 7th-rank tell

principles.prompt: Your king stands in front of your pawn, two ranks ahead of it. What's the verdict?
principles.answer: Winning, whoever moves — the headroom means you can always regain the opposition. (Rook pawns excepted.)

principles.prompt: Your king is in front of your pawn, but only one rank ahead. Who wins?
principles.answer: It hinges on the opposition: if the defender must move, you win; if you must move, it's a draw. On the 6th rank in front of the pawn you win regardless.

principles.prompt: You're defending, king in front of the pawn, and you're forced to give ground. Which way back?
principles.answer: Straight back on the pawn's file, never diagonally — so the pawn can only reach the 7th rank with check.

principles.prompt: The pawn steps to its 7th rank. Win or draw — what's the tell?
principles.answer: Check = draw: the defender slides in front and it's stalemate or the pawn falls. No check = win: the king shields the promotion square.

demos.title: The escort
demos.intro: White's king stands on the 6th rank in front of his pawn — a guaranteed win. Watch the escort bring it home.

steps.note: The king sidesteps. On the 6th in front of the pawn, this wins no matter whose move it is.
Black clings to the queening corner.
The pawn advances under full escort.
The moment that decides everything: the pawn hits the 7th WITHOUT check.
Black must step off the promotion square.
The king shields d8. Nothing stops the queen now.

demos.title: Straight back
demos.intro: Black's king holds the pawn's path. Played exactly, this is a draw — every move matters.

steps.note: Mirror. Every sidestep is answered in kind.
White spends his pawn move — but with the king beside the pawn, not in front, it gains nothing.
Now the pawn leans on the king directly.
Straight back — the move that saves the game. The diagonal retreats to d8 or f8 both lose.
White grabs the opposition — one square from victory.
But Black has the answer ready: oppose again.
The pawn arrives on the 7th WITH check — the drawing kind.
In front of it one last time.
Stalemate. Half a point for standing still — that's the whole defence.

tests.title: Bring it home
tests.intro: Your king is on the 6th, in front of the pawn — a won position. Prove it.

wrong.Kd5: You stepped out of the driver's seat — Black replies Ke7, covers every square in front of the pawn, and holds forever. Sidestep forward instead: Kd6 or Kf6.
wrong.Kf5: You stepped out of the driver's seat — Black replies Ke7, covers every square in front of the pawn, and holds forever. Sidestep forward instead: Kd6 or Kf6.

hints: The king leads. Which sidesteps keep it on the 6th rank, ahead of the pawn?
Kd6 or Kf6 — Black's king must give ground, and the pawn follows under escort.

tests.explanationAfter: Sidestep on the 6th, walk the pawn up behind the king, and land it on the 7th without check — then the king shields the promotion square. If your king ever drops back off the 6th, Black plants his king in front of the pawn and the win is gone.

tests.title: The saving square
tests.intro: White's king stands ready beside the pawn. You have exactly two legal moves — one draws, one loses.

wrong.Kd8: Wrong side! White answers Kf7, owns e8, and the pawn strolls in without a single check. Kf8 instead — it bars f7, and the only push left arrives with check.

hints: White wants Kf7 next, seizing the promotion square. Which retreat forbids it?
Kf8 — now e7 comes with check, and after Ke8 White has nothing better than stalemate.

tests.explanationAfter: Kf8 bars f7, so the pawn must arrive with check — and after e7+ Ke8, White must give stalemate or abandon the pawn. Kd8 hands White f7 and the e8 square: the pawn then walks in silently, and silent means winning.

tests.title: The full defence
tests.intro: White's king leads his pawn up the board. Hold the draw from here — every move is a test.

wrong.Kd8: Straight back is right later — right now White strides to d6, in front of his pawn, and wins. First bar his king: Ke7.
wrong.Kc6: You're abandoning the pawn's road — White plays Ke6, plants his king in front, and escorts it home. Ke7 holds the door.
wrong.Ke8: One rank too generous — White takes e6, in front of his pawn, and it's over. Stay close: Ke7, opposing his king.

hints: His king leads the pawn — yours must bar the road. Which square faces e5 with one gap?
Ke7 — take the opposition. Then mirror every sidestep, and when the pawn pushes you, retreat straight back.

tests.explanationAfter: The whole defence in one line: take the opposition, mirror each sidestep, re-block after every pawn push, retreat straight back — and when the pawn hits the 7th with check, slide in front for the stalemate. One diagonal retreat anywhere along the way and White's king claims the square in front.

tests.title: Your escort service
tests.intro: Same won position, your colours: king on its 6th, pawn behind. Bring it home for Black.

wrong.Kd4: Backwards is out of the driver's seat — White replies Ke2, covers every square in front of your pawn, and holds. Sidestep forward: Kd3 or Kf3.
wrong.Kf4: Backwards is out of the driver's seat — White replies Ke2, covers every square in front of your pawn, and holds. Sidestep forward: Kd3 or Kf3.

hints: Same technique as White's escort, upside down. Which sidesteps keep your king in front, on its 6th rank?
Kd3 or Kf3 — White's king must give ground, then the pawn follows you in.

tests.explanationAfter: The escort works identically in both directions: sidestep on your 6th rank, advance the pawn behind the king, land it on the 2nd without check, and shield e1 while it queens.
